comments_add: The ICA removed too much alpha activity (77.88%, above the 30% limit). It may have removed useful brain signals along with the noise. So, we will not use the ICA-cleaned file. We will use the cleaned EEG file from before ICA instead.

ICA removed too much alpha activity (63.7%, above the 30% limit) and reduced the signal variance by 99.8%. This suggests that too much of the original signal may have been lost. We will not use the ICA-cleaned file; we will use the cleaned EEG file from before ICA instead.

Posterior alpha loss (40.17%) exceeds the 30% guard. Despite strong ocular-artifact evidence for IC 3 and modest variance reduction, preservation of useful neural activity is not sufficiently established. Exclude the ICA output and use the cleaned pre-ICA *_eeg.fif file for subsequent feature extraction.

Posterior alpha loss (86.63%) substantially exceeds the 30% guard. Despite low overall variance reduction (4.56%), the ICA output shows severe loss of posterior alpha activity, raising substantial concern about the removal of useful neural signals. Exclude the ICA output and retain the cleaned pre-ICA *_eeg.fif file for subsequent feature extraction.

IC 5 shows a frontal-positive and posterior-negative scalp distribution consistent with a vertical ocular artifact. Its EOG correlation is moderate (0.537), providing supporting but not conclusive evidence of ocular activity. Posterior alpha loss (9.99%) and variance reduction (7.04%) remain within the specified acceptance guards. Approve the ICA-cleaned output, with the component identity documented as a visually supported ocular-artifact classification.

IC 0 and IC 1 show frontal scalp distributions consistent with ocular artifacts, supported by a high EOG correlation (0.883). Posterior alpha activity is preserved, with only a small reported change (-2.15%), and the variance reduction of 47.75% is consistent with substantial artifact removal. The low high-frequency fraction removed (0.7%) provides little evidence of significant muscle-band removal. Approve the ICA output, documenting the component classification as visually supported rather than definitive.

IC 2 shows a frontal scalp distribution consistent with an ocular artifact, while IC 5 shows a broad frontal distribution that may also be ocular-related. However, the supplied figures do not establish the individual component timecourses and frequency spectra clearly enough to exclude neural activity or muscle contamination confidently. Although alpha loss (10.56%) and variance reduction (18.09%) pass the specified guards, 10.3% high-frequency content removal warrants further component-level review. Keep the ICA output on hold until IC 2 and IC 5 are assessed individually.

The evidence does not conclusively confirm that all three removed components (IC2, IC3, IC4) are artifacts. Although the aggregate metrics pass the stated guards (12.8% alpha loss, 18.87% variance reduction, 0.8% high-frequency removal), these metrics alone cannot establish that removing all three components is safe. Keep the pre-ICA cleaned file as the fallback; ICA output not to be used, pending further component-level review.

IC0, IC1, and IC2 show frontal patterns consistent with possible ocular artifacts, and the aggregate EOG correlation of 0.930 supports this interpretation. However, the current figures do not conclusively verify all three exclusions. The 75.27% variance reduction is unusually large and requires careful review; passing alpha-loss (8.01%) and HF-removal (3.1%) guards does not establish that the exclusions are safe. ICA output not to be used; retain the pre-ICA cleaned file as the fallback, pending further component-level review.

IC0 has a strongly frontal scalp distribution and a high absolute EOG-proxy correlation of 0.962, supporting an ocular-artifact interpretation. Alpha loss is 14.2%, comfortably below the 30% guard; variance reduction is 41.64%, and HF removal is only 1.1%. The available waveform, component map, and quality metrics support the exclusion. Component-level evidence and metrics documented.

IC2 shows substantial low-frequency power compatible with ocular artifact, but also a visible peak around 10-11 Hz within the alpha band. Combined with the frontal scalp distribution and EOG-proxy correlation of -0.823, the evidence supports a possible ocular component but does not establish that it is purely ocular. Alpha loss is low at 5.0%, variance reduction is 11.07%, and only one artifact window was flagged, so the benefit of removal is uncertain; HF removal of 3.5% warrants a check for possible muscle content. Do not approve IC2 removal solely on the basis of the correlation or spectrum. ICA output not to be used; retain the pre-ICA cleaned file as the fallback, pending further review.

IC4 shows repeated sharp transients aligned with large frontal EOG-proxy peaks, supporting an ocular-artifact interpretation. The EOG correlation is 0.801, alpha loss is 11.55% (below the 30% guard), variance reduction is 1.65%, and HF removal is 0.5%. The low variance reduction is not a rejection criterion by itself. Approved with the component-level evidence documented; provisional framing of the review retained here.

IC2 has a frontal scalp distribution and EOG-proxy correlation of -0.79, supporting possible ocular contamination, but the displayed waveform does not conclusively establish a purely ocular component. Provisional framing of the review retained in this record.
